## What you will learn

- Which fundamentals this course **assumes** you already have from the robotics course (and the
  external links to revisit)
- Which fundamentals this course **teaches from zero** in its five foundations tracks (FA, FEL,
  FGL, FRA, FOP)
- How to use the cross-reference system: when a lesson says "cross-ref robotics 08", what to do

## Why it matters

You did the robotics course: ROS 2, frames, sensors, control, localization, SLAM, CV, ML. A lot of
that transfers to Hermon directly — and a lot does not. This course makes the split explicit so
you spend your time on the *delta* (the flying part) instead of re-learning what you know, and so
you don't skip a "robotics" lesson that is actually teaching you something drone-specific.

## Concept

### Assumed: what the robotics course already gave you

These come from `github.com/tal-giladi/robotics-course` (the sibling of this repo). The course
assumes you have done them and can answer their knowledge checks without notes:

| Topic | Robotics lesson | How Hermon uses it |
|---|---|---|
| ROS 2 basics (nodes, topics, services, QoS) | module 04 | 15.02, 15.03 (MAVROS) |
| Coordinate frames (TF, ENU vs robot frame) | module 05 | 13.07, FGL.04 |
| Sensors (time sync, latency, accuracy) | module 07 | 05.06, 14.09 |
| Control (PID, cascades, tuning) | module 08 | 07.03–07.06, P02 |
| Odometry (dead reckoning, error growth) | module 09 | 13.10 (GNSS-denied) |
| Localization (map matching, AMCL) | module 10 | 12.04 (home/RTL) |
| SLAM (mapping) | module 11 | 14.03 (field calibration) |
| Navigation (Nav2, costmaps) | module 12 | 15.06 (3D path planning) |
| Computer vision (pinhole, calibration) | module 13 | 14.02, 14.03 |
| ML (training, deployment, edge) | module 16 | 14.05 (YOLO), 14.10 (edge) |
| Units, kinematics (FP track) | FP.01 | FA.07 |
| Physics (forces, energy) | FM track | FA.01–FA.03 |

The rule: **if a drone lesson says "cross-ref robotics 08"**, it means "the PID/cascade mechanics
are the same — re-read robotics 08 for the tuning method, then read this lesson for the *air*
part (800 Hz, gyro noise, actuator lag)." The cross-reference is a *pointer*, not a substitute:
the drone lesson always contains the flying-specific delta.

### Taught from zero: the five foundations tracks

The robotics course's foundations (FM/FE/FP/FL/FPY/FC/FCT/FML/FCV/F3D) cover the *ground robot's*
physics, electronics, and perception. A flying machine needs five tracks the robotics course did
not teach (or taught only in passing). These live in `optional-foundations/` and are marked
**optional** in the syllabus: you may do them all, or skip them via the skip rule, or do them
just-in-time when the main lesson flags them.

| Track | Dir | Lessons | The delta vs robotics |
|---|---|---|---|
| **FA** — flight aerodynamics & physics | `optional-foundations/flight-aerodynamics/` | 8 | Vectors/Newton from zero (FA.01–02), work/energy (FA.03), trajectory trig (FA.04), **projectile motion** (FA.05 — the payload drop math), wind vectors (FA.06), units (FA.07), dimensional sanity (FA.08) |
| **FEL** — drone electronics & power | `optional-foundations/drone-electronics-power/` | 9 | Electricity refresher (FEL.01), DC power + wire gauges (FEL.02), **LiPo deep dive** (FEL.03 — cells, C-rating, sag), **BLDC from zero** (FEL.04), **DShot/CRSF** (FEL.05), **PDB/BEC design** (FEL.06), fuses (FEL.07), power measurement/shunts (FEL.08), **battery storage/transport** (FEL.09 — US summers, customs) |
| **FGL** — GNSS & navigation math | `optional-foundations/gnss-navigation-math/` | 7 | Datums/geoid (FGL.01), WGS84 + local frames (FGL.02), UTM (FGL.03), **ENU/NED** (FGL.04 — which one ArduPilot uses), haversine/geodesy (FGL.05), **satellite geometry/DOP** (FGL.06), **GPS time/atomic clocks** (FGL.07) |
| **FRA** — RF & datalink | `optional-foundations/rf-datalink/` | 8 | RF in 45 min (FRA.01 — dB, dBm, wavelength), **link budget math** (FRA.02), antennas/polarization (FRA.03), spread spectrum 2.4 GHz (FRA.04), 5.8 GHz video (FRA.05), **SBUS/CRSF/MAVLink layers** (FRA.06), interference (FRA.07), **US regulatory bands** (FRA.08) |
| **FOP** — civil & ops | `optional-foundations/civil-ops/` | 7 | **Civil org & rank** (FOP.01), **OPORD/METTLE** (FOP.02), **mission planning process** (FOP.03), airspace concepts (FOP.04), **comms brevity codes** (FOP.05), **risk management: bowtie** (FOP.06), **AAR/debrief** (FOP.07) |

The bold rows are the ones with no robotics equivalent at all — FA.05 (projectile motion is the
canister drop math, 17.07), FGL.06–07 (satellite geometry and GPS time are the GNSS module's
math), FRA.02/06/08 (link budgets, protocol layers, US bands), and all of FOP (the robotics
course had no ops track — you are heading toward an FAA job).

### How the optional system works

Each main lesson's `optional` field lists the foundations lessons that would help. The rule is
uniform:

- **The main lesson is self-contained.** You can do every main lesson without any foundations
  lesson — the main lesson teaches the minimum the flying machine needs.
- **The foundations lesson goes deeper.** If a main lesson says "wind math: FA.06", the main
  lesson shows the wind case it needs; FA.06 teaches the vector math generally, with exercises.
- **The skip rule is per-lesson.** `course.py skip` checks each foundations lesson's
  `skip_if` statement independently. You are not "doing FA" or "skipping FA" — you skip or do
  *each lesson* on its own statement.

> [!TIP]
> **Ask your teacher:** "I did robotics modules 08 and 12 thoroughly. Which drone lessons can I
> do faster because of that, and which will still be slow because the air part is new?"

## Technical explanation

### Level 1 — Intuition: transfer is partial, and the delta is the course

You know how to tune a PID for a wheel. Hermon's rate loop is a PID for a *gyro* at 800 Hz with
a 5 ms actuator lag — the mechanics are the same, the numbers and the failure modes are not. You
know localization on a map. Hermon's "map" is 3D, moving (wind), and partly fake (multipath).
The pattern is: **the robotics course taught you the machinery; this course teaches you the
flying delta.** The cross-reference marks tell you exactly where the machinery ends and the delta
begins.

### Level 2 — Practical: the three cross-reference types

| Marker in a lesson | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| "cross-ref robotics 08" | The machinery is robotics lesson 08; the delta is below | Re-read robotics 08 (10 min), then do this lesson |
| "FA.05 (optional)" | A foundations lesson goes deeper; the main lesson is self-contained | Skip unless the main lesson's exercise needs the general math |
| "FOP.02 (optional)" | A ops-context lesson; not needed for the aircraft | Do it if you want the ops language (18 uses it constantly) |

### Level 3 — Mathematics: where the math is new

The robotics course's math (kinematics, PID, Kalman, homography, CNN backprop) is all reused.
The *new* math in this course is small and specific:

- **Thrust/force balance and tilt** (01.01, FA.02) — $T\cos\theta = mg$, $T\sin\theta = ma$
- **Projectile motion** (FA.05, 17.07) — drop time, lead, release point
- **Link budget** (FRA.02, 09.05) — dBm, FSPL, margin
- **Geodesy** (FGL.05) — haversine, great-circle
- **DOP** (FGL.06) — dilution of precision from satellite geometry

Everything else (Kalman, PID, YOLO, ROS 2) is a reuse with new numbers. That is the honest
scope of the "new" part of this course.

### Level 4 — Implementation: the repo layout

Both repos are the same shape (docsify + `course.py` + `curriculum/syllabus.yaml` +
`tools/build.py`/`validate.py`). The robotics course's foundations live in
`optional-foundations/{physics,electronics,signals,...}`; this course's in
`optional-foundations/{flight-aerodynamics,drone-electronics-power,gnss-navigation-math,rf-datalink,civil-ops}`.
The cross-references use relative links (`../optional-foundations/...`) within this repo and
absolute URLs to `github.com/tal-giladi/robotics-course` across repos.

## Code

Save as `transfer_check.py` and run `python transfer_check.py`. Standard library only.

```python
"""00.05 — the transfer check: which robotics lessons does each drone module rely on,
and which foundations track fills the gap? A quick self-audit before you start.
"""
# module -> (robotics lessons assumed, foundations tracks that fill the gap)
PLAN = {
    "01 flight physics":   ("FM (partially)", ["FA"]),
    "02 motors/escs/props": ("FE (partially)", ["FEL", "FA"]),
    "03 power":            ("FE (partially)", ["FEL"]),
    "05 sensing":          ("07 sensors", ["FEL"]),
    "06 estimation":       ("10 localization (partially)", ["FGL"]),
    "07 control":          ("08 control", ["FA", "FRA"]),
    "09 link":             ("—", ["FRA"]),
    "13 GNSS":             ("05 frames, 10 localization", ["FGL"]),
    "14 vision":           ("13 CV, 16 ML", ["FRA"]),
    "15 onboard autonomy": ("04 ROS 2, 08 control, 12 navigation", []),
    "17 payload":          ("13 CV, 16 ML", ["FA"]),
    "18 ops":              ("—", ["FOP"]),
}


def audit(done_robotics: set[str]) -> None:
    print(f"Robotics lessons done (per your self-audit): {sorted(done_robotics)}\n")
    gaps = 0
    for mod, (assumed, tracks) in PLAN.items():
        missing = [a for a in assumed.replace(" (partially)", "").split(",")
                   if a.strip() and a.strip() != "—" and a.strip() not in done_robotics]
        mark = "OK " if not missing else "GAP"
        if missing:
            gaps += 1
        print(f"[{mark}] {mod:24s} assumed: {assumed:28s} foundations: {', '.join(tracks) or '—'}")
        for m in missing:
            print(f"       missing: robotics {m} — re-read it, or let the drone lesson teach the minimum")
    print(f"\n{gaps} modules have an assumed-lesson gap. A gap is not a blocker: the drone")
    print("lesson teaches the minimum; the robotics lesson teaches the machinery in depth.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Edit this set to match what you actually did in the robotics course.
    # The default assumes the full core path.
    done = {"04", "05", "07", "08", "09", "10", "11", "12", "13", "16"}
    audit(done)
```

## Expected result

- **00.05-E1:** The exact gaps depend on your audit — the skill is naming the *first exposure*:
  e.g. "I skipped robotics 16 (ML) → 14.05 (YOLO) will expose it when I have to read a model's
  latency profile" or "I did robotics 08 but only in sim → 07.11 (measured step response) will
  expose the tuning gap when the real motor's lag shows up."
- **00.05-E2:** 07.03: same as robotics 08 (PID, cascade, Ziegler–Nichols as a starting point);
  new: 800 Hz sample rate, gyro bias/drift, the actuator lag (5 ms) that the robotics motor
  (0.08 s) did not have, and the stability constraint (a wrong gain doesn't just oscillate, it
  flips the aircraft). 13.02: same as robotics 10's "estimate from sensors" idea; new: the
  trilateration is in 3D with 4+ satellites, a clock bias term, and the errors are ionosphere/
  multipath, not sensor noise. 15.06: same as robotics 12 (A*/RRT, costmaps); new: the space is
  3D, the obstacles move (wind is not an obstacle, the target is), and the replan rate is
  constrained by the aircraft's turn radius, not by the robot's.
- **00.05-E3:** (a) 33 h / 342 h ≈ **9.6 %**. (b) The bold set is 15 lessons ≈ **12.5 h**; the
  modules that benefit most: 17 (FA.05 → the drop math), 13 (FGL.06/07 → the GNSS math), 09
  (FRA.02/08 → the link), 18 (FOP → the ops language). (c) A reasonable first three: FEL.03
  (LiPo — the battery is in your hand in module 02 and it will be in the air in 11), FA.05
  (projectile — you will use it in 17 but the math is 30 min and it unblocks the whole payload
  module), FRA.04 (bands — before you buy the SiK radio in 09, know which window is legal
  band).

## Troubleshooting

### Symptom: the audit says OK but a drone lesson feels hard

"Done" in the robotics course means the knowledge check passed, not that the skill is fluent. A
hard drone lesson is usually a *fluency* gap (you know the PID, you cannot tune one in 20 min) —
the fix is to re-do the robotics lesson's *practical challenge*, not the whole module.

### Symptom: a cross-reference link to the robotics course is broken

The robotics course lives at `github.com/tal-giladi/robotics-course`; if you have it locally, the
link should resolve relative to that repo. If not, open the URL directly — the lessons are
published, not just in the git repo.

## Common mistakes

- **Treating "assumed" as "taught".** The course assumes you *know* ROS 2; it will not re-teach
  nodes and topics. If 15.02 feels like Greek, that is a robotics 04 gap, not a drone-course gap.
- **Doing all 39 foundations lessons up front.** They are optional and just-in-time. Doing 33 h of
  foundations before module 02 delays the build by a month — the skip rule exists so you do only
  what the flying needs, when it needs it.
- **Skipping foundations because "I did robotics".** The delta rows (FA.05, FGL.06/07, FRA.02/08,
  all of FOP) have no robotics equivalent. "I did robotics" covers the machinery, not the delta.
- **Cross-referencing in one direction only.** The robotics course has no drone lessons; when you
  hit a drone concept that generalizes (e.g. ENU/NED frames), note it for the robotics course —
  the two repos are siblings and the cross-links should stay honest.

## Knowledge check

1. Name two topics the course assumes from the robotics course and two it teaches from zero.
   <details><summary>Answer</summary>

   Assumed: ROS 2 (robotics 04), control/PID (robotics 08), CV (13), ML (16). From zero:
   projectile motion (FA.05), LiPo/BLDC/DShot (FEL.03–05), GNSS math (FGL.06/07), RF link budget
   (FRA.02), civil ops (FOP).
   </details>

2. A lesson says "cross-ref robotics 08" and also lists "FRA.05 (optional)". What do you do?
   <details><summary>Answer</summary>

   Re-read robotics 08 (the machinery), do this lesson (the delta), and skip FRA.05 unless the
   lesson's exercise needs 5.8 GHz video specifics (FRA.05 is the 5.8 GHz video lesson — optional
   depth, not required).
   </details>

3. Why are the five foundations tracks marked optional instead of required?
   <details><summary>Answer</summary>

   Because every main lesson is self-contained: the main lesson teaches the minimum the flying
   machine needs. The foundations go deeper and are just-in-time. Making them required would add
   33 h up front and delay the build; the per-lesson skip rule lets a strong background skip most
   of them and a weak background do all of them.
   </details>

4. The audit flags a gap at robotics 13 (CV) and you are at drone module 14. What is the cheapest
   fix?
   <details><summary>Answer</summary>

   Re-do robotics 13's practical challenge (the calibration one — it is the one 14.03 reuses) and
   read robotics 13's "pinhole model" section (10 min), then continue drone 14. The full robotics
   13 module is not needed — the drone lesson teaches the UAV delta and the robotics lesson
   supplies the machinery.
   </details>

5. Which foundations track has *no* robotics-course equivalent at all, and why does the course
   still include it?
   <details><summary>Answer</summary>

   FOP (civil & ops fundamentals) — the robotics course had no ops track, and this
   course ends in an FAA job: the OPORD (FOP.02), the mission-planning process (FOP.03), the
   comms brevity (FOP.05), the bowtie risk method (FOP.06) and the AAR (FOP.07) are the
   operator's working language in module 18 and the capstone.
   </details>
